name: Bump Stops, Packers & Droop Limiters
description: Jounce bumpers on the front strut and rear shock shafts, packers/spacers that set when the bump stop engages, and droop limiters. On a lowered race car the bump stop is a tuning element (it is effectively a rising-rate spring), not just a crash stop.

components.name: Front jounce bumper (bump stop) and dust boot
components.description: Microcellular urethane bump stop on the front strut rod inside the dust boot ('front shock absorber boot with jounce bumper', reused when changing struts per GM). When lowering, cut-down or shorter progressive race bump stops keep the car from riding on the stop mid-corner.
components.location: On front strut rod under the top mount, approx (x 0.045, y 0.76, z +/-0.57).

factory.name: GM front shock absorber boot with jounce bumper

raceOptions.name: Race bump rubber (progressive) from damper manufacturer
raceOptions.notes: Choose length/stiffness with the damper builder; measure shaft travel with a zip-tie on the rod.

installNotes: With spring removed, cycle suspension to full bump and record shaft travel to bump-stop contact and to tire/fender contact.
inspection: Zip-tie on shaft to log max travel each session.

components.name: Rear jounce bumper and shock boot
components.description: Bump stop on the rear shock rod, transferred to replacement shocks (GM SG3). Because of the LCA motion ratio, rear shock shaft travel is less than wheel travel; size the stop accordingly.
components.location: Upper rear shock shaft, approx (x 2.76, y 0.64, z +/-0.58).

factory.name: GM rear shock absorber jounce bumper + boot

images.title: GM Gen 6 Camaro rear suspension exploded diagram: 5 links, knuckle with 3 bushings, shock, spring, stabilizer, cradle with 4 mounts

modelRef.features: Foam jounce bumper on the shock rod under the upper mount, inside the shock boot (item 8)

components.name: Bump stop packers / spacers
components.description: Thin spacer washers (typically 2-5 mm) stacked on the damper shaft above the bump stop to bring forward bump-stop engagement without changing the bump stop itself. Used for fine aero platform control and to tune balance (more front packer = earlier front stop engagement = more understeer under heavy load).
components.location: On damper rods under the top mounts.

raceOptions.name: Split packer washers sized to shaft

installNotes: Document packer stack on setup sheet per corner.

components.name: Droop (rebound) limiters
components.description: Internal damper droop spacers or external limit straps that limit extension. Used to reduce inside-wheel lift and control weight transfer/aero pitch; also prevents CV/halfshaft overextension at the rear and protects brake hoses and wheel-speed-sensor leads at full droop.
components.location: Inside dampers (internal spacer) or between body and LCA/knuckle (strap).

raceOptions.name: Internal droop spacers (built by damper manufacturer)

installNotes: Check that at full droop the brake hoses, WSS leads and halfshaft angles are within limits.
